title: KMS & HSM Evidence Automation + SIEM Export Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures our operational approach for integrating KMS/HSM key management with RBAC v2, structured audit logging, evidence automation for compliance requests, and SIEM export best practices. It focuses on encryption-at-rest patterns (DEK+KEK/envelope), BYOK ingestion paths, rotation procedures (scheduled and emergency), and how to produce tamper-evident artifacts that auditors and customers can consume.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: security engineers, platform ops, SRE on-call, compliance engineers, and solutions engineering for enterprise BYOK onboarding.
- Scope: Hosted + Dedicated + Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) where Redwood either manages keys (KMS) or integrates customer-supplied keys (BYOK/HSM).

High-level architecture (summary):
- DEKs (data encryption keys) are generated per-customer/tenant and encrypted (wrapped) with a KEK stored in KMS or HSM.
- For BYOK/HSM, a customer-provided root KEK is imported or sealed behind an HSM-backed KEK abstraction.
- Envelope encryption is used for blobs, DB rows, and cache material where applicable.
- A lightweight key-metadata service tracks key_id, key_version, rotation_state, origin (redwood-kms | customer-byo | external-hsm), and last_rotated_ts.

RBAC v2 mappings for key operations (recommended):
- roles: key-admin, key-operator, key-reader, auditor, app-service
- key-admin: create/import BYOK, schedule rotations, change policy, set admin metadata. (principle-of-least-privilege; MFA-required)
- key-operator: perform rotation workflows, kick off emergency rotations, run key health checks.
- key-reader: metadata read only, used by config dashboards and support tools.
- auditor: read-only access to audit logs and evidence artifacts, no access to key material or unwrap operations.
- app-service: unwrap/wrap capability for runtime services, constrained by usage quotas and network policy (only allowed from service CIDRs).

Notes on RBAC integration:
- Map RBAC v2 roles to IAM principals using short-lived service tokens where possible. Avoid long-lived static credentials for app-service unwrap operations.
- Document a default deny policy for any key unless explicitly granted.
- Time-bound grants for emergency rotation windows (e.g., 4-hour elevated window), recorded in audit log as "elevation_event".

Audit log schema (canonical JSON schema for KMS/HSM events):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- event_type: one of [KEY_CREATE, KEY_IMPORT, KEY_ROTATE_START, KEY_ROTATE_END, KEY_ROTATE_FAIL, KEY_DEPRECATE, KEY_DELETE, KEY_UNWRAP, KEY_WRAP, KEY_ACCESS_DENIED, ELEVATION_EVENT]
- actor: principal id (service account or user email)
- actor_role: RBAC role at time of event
- key_id: canonical key identifier (kms://redwood/keys/<id> or hsm://<slot>/<id>)
- key_version: string
- operation: human friendly action (e.g., "unwrap_dek", "rotate_keK", "import_byo_key")
- result: success | failure | partial
- request_id: opaque UUID for correlation across services
- correlation_id: trace id for distributed tracing
- source_ip: IP of caller (if available)
- region: region or datacenter id
- kms_provider: redwood-kms | aws-kms | azure-kv | pkcs11-hsm
- hsm_attestation: boolean (true if HSM attestation included)
- attestation_blob: base64-url (present when hsm_attestation true)
- algorithm: AES-256-GCM | RSA-OAEP | RSA-PSS etc.
- key_length: bits as string (e.g., "256")
- rotation_trigger: schedule | manual | compromise-detected | cust-request
- notes: free-form short message

Practical examples (single-line JSON log for SIEM):
{"timestamp":"2025-01-09T20:13:02Z","event_type":"KEY_ROTATE_END","actor":"svc-keyops@redwood.ai","actor_role":"key-operator","key_id":"kms://redwood/keys/abc123","key_version":"v3","operation":"rotate_kek","result":"success","request_id":"5b3c6a8f-1a2b-4c2d-9ef0-8a7b6c1d2e3f","correlation_id":"trace-0a1b2c","source_ip":"34.122.10.88","region":"us-west1","kms_provider":"redwood-kms","hsm_attestation":"false","algorithm":"AES-256-GCM","key_length":"256","rotation_trigger":"schedule","notes":"auto-rotation window success"}

SIEM export patterns and advice:
- Deliver audit events as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) to allow Elastic/Kibana and Datadog ingestion without parsing issues.
- Push model: agent forwards to log-collector -> log-forwarder -> SIEM endpoint (TLS + mutual auth for private deployments).
- Pull model: SIEM queries an export API with a time-bounded token; this is useful for enterprise SIEM that prefers polling.
- Tags to include for quick search: team, env (prod/staging), tenancy (customer-id), key_origin (redwood | byo), retention_tier.
- Recommended retention: 2y primary hot (for compliance queries), 7y archived (cold) for regulated customers.

Evidence automation (what to collect and why):
- For rotation events collect: rotation start log, rotation end log with result, new key_version identifier, attestation_blob (if HSM), checksum of wrapped key material, signed operation token (KMS signs the rotation record).
- For BYOK imports: store customer-signed import manifest, HSM import confirmation, import_request_id, and copy of the acceptance policy.
- For decryptability proof: generate a small signed test vector (encrypted with new key, decrypt performed in controlled environment, result hash signed by KMS/HSM) and include in evidence bundle.
- Store evidence bundles as immutable objects (append-only) in a compliance bucket (S3/GCS) with object-lock or WORM when supported. Name convention: evidence/<customer-id>/<key-id>/<rotation_ts>-bundle.jsonl.gpg

Automated evidence pipeline (recommended flow):
1) Rotation completes -> key-metadata service emits rotation_end event -> event triggers Evidence Orchestrator lambda (or k8s job)
2) Orchestrator collects logs, attestation blobs, signed test vector, and policy snapshots
3) Generate a signed ZIP (pgp/GPG) and a JSONL manifest with SHA256 digests
4) Push to compliance bucket and attach an immutable ticket in Jira (SEC- evidence) with pointers and automated email to compliance owner
5) Send metadata to SIEM for indexing (do not include private key material)

Encryption-at-rest design decisions (short rationale):
- Envelope encryption to limit expensive KMS calls per data operation: DEKs cached locally for short TTLs, but DEKs never persisted in plain text to long-term storage.
- KEKs in HSM for customers who require FIPS-level attestation; Redwood-managed KMS for typical customers.
- Use AEAD algorithms (AES-GCM) for object storage and database cell encryption to provide integrity.
- For low-latency workloads (embedding cache, ephemeral caches), prefer local DEK caches; require periodic re-wrap events and audit.

Key rotation procedures (operational playbook):
- Scheduled rotation (quarterly default for DEKs, yearly for KEKs unless stronger SLAs requested):
  - PRE: create next_version KEK, run canary unwrap/wrap tests on staging, update key metadata as PREPARED -> schedule window, notify stakeholders
  - DURING: enter rotation window, switch wrapping policy so new DEKs are wrapped with new KEK while existing wrapped DEKs remain readable by previous KEK versions for a defined overlap (grace period). Record every step in audit logs.
  - POST: run bulk rewrap of long-lived artifacts in background, validate checksums, update metadata to mark previous version deprecated.
- Emergency rotation (compromise suspected):
  - Immediately create new KEK version, push immediate unwrap-block policy for old KEK for suspicious actor containment (if safe), and start forced rewrap. Notify legal/compliance. Use pre-approved emergency runbook with time-limited RBAC elevation.
  - Produce an evidence bundle marked "emergency" with a complete timeline and all relevant logs.

Rollback and fallbacks:
- Rolling back a KEK rotation is only possible if the old KEK version still exists and attestation confirms integrity. Because of wrap/unwrap immutability constraints, prefer multi-version support rather than full rollback.
- If rewrap fails at scale, failover to read-only mode and surface a customer-impact dashboard, escalate to SRE and solutions engineering.

Testing and verification checklist (pre-release and periodic audits):
- Unit tests for wrap/unwrap across all supported algorithms/providers.
- Integration tests for BYOK import path with HSM simulated attestation.
- Chaos test: simulate KMS throttling and verify fallback to cached DEKs and service degradation behavior.
- Daily smoke: run nightly canary that performs a wrap/unwrap and stores proof in evidence bucket.

Operational notes and gotchas:
- Do not include plaintext key material in logs or evidence bundles. Always include digests and signed attestations.
- Attestation blobs can be large; compress and index by hash to avoid duplicate storage.
- SIEM ingestion must redact any field flagged as sensitive by our PII/data-classification service.
- For private/on-prem BYOK, recommend mutual TLS + mTLS client cert rotate policy for forwarder services.

Open questions / action items:
- Q1: Minimum HSM attestation format we will accept from third-party partners — propose and align by Feb 2025. Owner: Evan Carter.
- Q2: Retention policy differences for EU-regulated customers vs general policy (GDPR interplay with long-term archives). Owner: Lena Ortiz.
- Q3: Extension to token-level cost telemetry for unwrap operations to feed Optimize. Owner: Marcus Zhou.

Appendix: sample commands and small scripts
- Example: generate evidence manifest snippet (bash pseudocode):
  - curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVID_TOKEN" "https://platform.redwood.ai/api/keys/abc123/rotation/manifest" > manifest.json
  - gpg --encrypt --recipient compliance@redwood.ai -o evidence-20250109.zip.gpg ./collected/*

References:
- Confluence: KMS Design Index (linked above)
- GitHub: PRs that changed the key-metadata service (linked above)
- Jira: SEC-4980 emergency rotation retrofit

Notes-to-self (rough):

End of playbook (working draft).
